newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique seeks $859 mln in credits, debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique seeks $859 mln in credits, debt relief.

text.p: Mozambique will be seeking pledges of about $859 million in credit, grants and debt relief at a meeting of the World Bank's consultative group on the country, the Maputo daily Noticias reported on Saturday.
Prime Minister Pascoal Mocumbi told the newspaper he would present this figure at the annual meeting in Paris next week, to be attended by donor governments and bankers.

Mozambique will be asking for credits of $307 million and grants of $334 million. The government also hopes the consultative group will cancel at least $25 million in debt and reschedule a further $193 million owed.
Mozambique, one of the world's poorest nations, has been implementing a World Bank-supported economic structural adjustment programme since 1987.
The southern African nation received pledges of $881 million at the Paris meeting last year, but recent government figures showed that $953 million had actually been received.
